## How the score was worked out

Each result implies a score on its own, after adjusting for how hard that test is and who ran it. The model's score is their weighted average, with a small pull toward the middle for thinly tested models. Each test's weight is its *counts* column above; here it is added up by who ran the tests. [Method](../method.md)

<pre>
source                                   results  share of the score

prior: pull toward the middle                       1% ▇
weighted average                                  = 55.0
</pre>

## How to run it

### Other ways to run it

1. Run it as published (BF16-T1E, needs ~68.7 GB, NVIDIA only, from [huggingface.co/frontier-infra](https://huggingface.co/frontier-infra/jebadiah-27b-v2-1/blob/b1df30c3cd9ad97c31ddb0b7c6884b580876bcdd/README.md))
   
   ```sh
   pip install torch==2.8.0 transformers==5.17.0 accelerate safetensors git+https://github.com/apolinario/decision-index.git@25c6ec7b6b5f44a216c63c3a700de3a9c6d6699d && git clone https://github.com/getainode/jebadiah.git jebadiah-t1e && git -C jebadiah-t1e checkout 678f6e2cc2bb1b51f34407d00255b5e13109ce3f && PYTHONPATH=jebadiah-t1e/eval/decision-index python -c 'from jebadiah_engine import JebadiahEngine; e=JebadiahEngine(model="frontier-infra/jebadiah-27b-v2-1", revision="e38b48b82bcda8943d0958072c042c5867284838", device="cuda", dtype="bfloat16", repeat_payload=True, reverse_avg_below=0.7, prefix_cache=True, max_batch=64, batch_tokens=32768); print(e("The invoice is overdue.", {"overdue":{"type":"noul","instructions":"Is the invoice overdue?"}}))'
   ```
